fixes.explanation: Paul writes, "I became a servant of this gospel by the gift of God’s grace…" (Ephesians 3:7). A gift, friend. He doesn't say he earned the job. The work came to him as grace, given through the working of God's power.

Law is a big word in the Bible, but it's not the one Paul uses here. He says, "I became a servant of this gospel by the gift of God’s grace…" (Ephesians 3:7). A gift is something handed to you, not something you earn. Paul's service started with what God gave him, and that's the word for the blank.

Covenant is a strong word, but it doesn't go in this blank. Paul says, "I became a servant of this gospel by the gift of God’s grace…" (Ephesians 3:7). He calls his service a gift. His place in the work came from what God gave him, and that's grace.

Paul says it "…for ages past was kept hidden in God, who created all things." (Ephesians 3:9). It was hidden in God, friend. Now Paul's job is to shine a light on it. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I'll tell you, a light is a lot better than the dark.

Paul doesn't mention the temple here. He says it "…for ages past was kept hidden in God, who created all things." (Ephesians 3:9). The mystery wasn't tucked away in a building. It was hidden in God Himself, the One who made all things.

Paul says, "His purpose was that now, through the church, the manifold wisdom of God should be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms…" (Ephesians 3:10). The heavenly realms, friend. Think about that. The church is how that wisdom gets made known to them.

Paul says it was "…the eternal purpose that He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord." (Ephesians 3:11). Eternal, friend. God didn't just have this purpose, He accomplished it in Christ Jesus. That's worth celebrating, and I'd say it's worth a whole batch of cookies.

Paul says, "So I ask you not to be discouraged because of my sufferings for you, which are your glory." (Ephesians 3:13). That's his request, friend. I think it's a tender thing to ask. He's the one in a hard spot, and I think he's still thinking about them.

Paul says it right at the end of the verse: "…my sufferings for you, which are your glory." (Ephesians 3:13). Your glory, friend. I won't pretend to explain more than he does there. I'll just say he said it, and I think he said it kindly.
